textile.reason: A woven cedar-bark and grass mat attributed to the Ahousaht, a Nuu-chah-nulth First Nation group, matching the claimed ethnicity and a well-documented traditional craft.

instruments.name: rattle
instruments.title: rattle
instruments.reason: A carved and painted wooden bird-form rattle with classic Northwest Coast formline design (black/red, whale/human motif), consistent with Nuu-chah-nulth/West Coast style regalia used in ceremonial dance.

instruments.name: rattle
instruments.title: rattle
instruments.reason: A carved wooden bird-form rattle with engraved human-face ornament, consistent with Nuu-chah-nulth/Northwest Coast carved ceremonial rattles used with dance and song; museum attributes it directly to Nuu-chah-nulth.

instruments.name: rattle
instruments.title: rattle
instruments.reason: A carved alder wood rattle in Thunderbird form, made by John Jacobsen of Ahousaht, a Nuu-chah-nulth group — a classic Northwest Coast instrument used in ceremonial dance.

instruments.name: rattle
instruments.title: rattle
instruments.reason: A bird-shaped rattle of painted alder wood with skin ties, a classic Northwest Coast ceremonial instrument type, and the museum records it as made by the Nuu-chah-nulth.

instruments.name: rattle

instruments.reason: A carved wooden bird-shaped rattle with worn traces of painted design and a handle, consistent with Northwest Coast Nuu-chah-nulth ceremonial rattles used in dance and ritual.
